title: Hymns of the Samaveda
dateDisplay: c. 1200–800 BCE (the collection is older than its surviving schools)
attributionNote: The Samaveda has no single author. Its verses are drawn almost entirely from the Rigveda and arranged for sung ritual, with the Soma sacrifice at the centre; the melodies were transmitted orally and are not fully recoverable from the printed text.
description: The Samaveda is the Veda of chant. Its verses, most of them Rigvedic, are set out in the order the Udgatri priest sings them at the Soma sacrifice, grouped into decades and books with the melodies' names noted. Griffith's translation gives the hymns in their liturgical order with a popular commentary, so the collection reads as a handbook of Vedic ritual song rather than as a sequence of poems.
historicalContext: The Samaveda as it survives belongs to the Kauthuma and Ranayaniya schools and is the basis of the later Samavedic chant traditions of Gujarat, Maharashtra and South India. Ralph T. H. Griffith published this translation with a popular commentary in 1895; it remains the standard complete English rendering of the collection.
availabilityNote: Complete. Griffith's translation and commentary are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time; the archive serves the work as one page, so the library splits it at the fifteen printed books — First Part, Books I–VI, and Second Part, Books I–IX — and serves one book per chapter. The volume's preface and the running commentary printed with the hymns are part of the page.
